title: Super source follower
description: A super source follower (SSF): a plain source follower whose output resistance is driven down by a local feedback device. The input follower sets the DC level shift (the output sits about one input $V_{GS}$ below the input), and the feedback device senses the follower current and closes a local loop that lowers the output resistance by roughly the feedback device's intrinsic gain: $R_{out} \approx 1/(g_{m,in} * A_{v0,fb})$, versus $1/g_{m,in}$ for a plain follower. That makes it a compact low-impedance buffer. The feedback is a local loop; its own phase margin (whether that loop is stable) is a small-signal AC check the simulator owns, out of this sheet's scope — this sheet sizes the DC operating point and the low-frequency output resistance only. On the demo NMOS table both devices size against the same data.

doc.title: Input follower device
doc.description: The source-follower input device carrying a fixed current; its gm sets the base output resistance and its vgs the DC level shift.

doc.title: Feedback device
doc.description: The local-feedback device that senses the follower current; its intrinsic gain av0 is the loop gain that lowers the output resistance.
